source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12 ("Derry local elections: nominations received")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: BNL 22 Apr 1927 p12 'Coleraine', read in the block image (areas 7-8): nominations, 'There will be no contest in any of the electoral divisions'.

note: Triennial election of Coleraine rural district (21 divisions, one member each). Nominations were received on 21 April 1927; there was no contest in any division (Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12). Eighteen members were returned unopposed. No nomination was received for Articlave (previous member James Millen), Bovagh (H. Y. Henderson) or Drumcroon (James Mairs); the previous members continued in office, as the Northern Whig's list (30 April 1927, p. 9) prints, and are recorded from reports of the new council's meetings (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Polled Friday 27 May 1927: 'Polling took place yesterday in the Bellarena division of county Londonderry, the only division in the county where there was a contest' for the county council (Londonderry Sentinel, Saturday 28 May 1927, p. 8), and the Limavady rural contest in Straw 'took place on Friday' (Derry Journal, 30 May 1927, p. 8). Returned unopposed.
